idiom_name: sealed interface DomainEvent + private MutableSharedFlow<DomainEvent> exposed as SharedFlow
implementation_notes: Kotlin's own idioms replace the classic registry: the closed event set is a sealed interface with data-class implementations, so when over it is exhaustive at compile time, and kotlinx.coroutines' MutableSharedFlow (private backing property, read-only SharedFlow view) is the documented event bus, emitting to all active collectors. Handlers are collect blocks scoped to an application or UI scope, which replaces subscription bookkeeping with structured-concurrency lifecycle. Requires the kotlinx-coroutines-core dependency (Kotlin 1.4+ for SharedFlow).
pitfalls: MutableSharedFlow() has replay = 0: an event emitted while nothing is collecting is lost - fine for one-shot UI signals, wrong for events that must drive state; use durable storage or a buffered Channel when exactly-once handoff to one consumer is required.
The collector's scope owns the subscription, so cancelling it silently unsubscribes; bus subscribers must be launched in a scope that outlives the request.

variants.name: Sealed hierarchy + typed handler registry (no coroutines)
variants.idiom_name: sealed interface + Map<KClass<out DomainEvent>, List<(DomainEvent) -> Unit>>
variants.implementation_notes: The synchronous, framework-free realization: when over the sealed hierarchy keeps compile-time exhaustiveness for direct dispatch, while an explicit registry of typed handlers (a map from event type to handler list) keeps the open/closed property for runtime registration. Choose it when reactions must run inside the caller's transaction and no coroutine infrastructure is wanted; the exhaustiveness guarantee then covers the event set, not the handler list, so pair registration with a startup check that every event type has a handler.
pitfalls: e::class matches the concrete class only, so a handler registered for a supertype silently never fires for subtypes - register per event type or walk the hierarchy.
Handlers are lambdas captured in a mutable map; an anonymous handler registered per request leaks unless it is removed explicitly.
